items.text: Criterion for accessibility of a category
$C\subset E$ small, strictly generating: every $X$ has a strictly epimorphic family $X_i\to X$, $X_i\in C$ (equivalently, $X$ a direct limit of objects of $C$).
We want the family to stay strictly epimorphic after any base change (universal). Automatic in a topos.
(i) fibre products exist in $E$; (ii) kernels of double arrows exist and
(u,v)\mapsto\operatorname{Ker}(u,v)\quad\text{is an accessible functor}
E.g. filtering direct limits commute with finite inverse limits. True for every topos.
Then every object of $E$ is accessible (SGA 4, I, 9.11), hence $E$ is accessible. Example: topoi.
Counterexample: $\mathbf{Ens}^{\circ}$
$\mathbf{Ens}^\circ$ has direct limits and a generator (a two-point set cogenerates $\mathbf{Ens}$), but is not accessible.
X\ \text{co-accessible in }\mathbf{Ens}\iff Y\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(Y,X)\ \text{turns large inverse limits into direct limits}\iff |X|\le1
A filtering set large with respect to $\pi$:
J=\{I'\subset I:\ |I'|\le\pi\}\subset\mathcal P(I),\quad \text{ordered by inclusion, } \pi\text{-dominating}\ (\pi\ \text{infinite})
A union of $\le\pi$ subsets of size $\le\pi$ has size $\le\pi$. If $|I|\le\pi$ then $J$ has a last element (uninteresting).
\prod_{i\in I}Y_i=\varprojlim_{I'\in J}Y_{I'},\qquad Y_{I'}=\prod_{i\in I'}Y_i
If $X$ were $\pi$-co-accessible, every map $\prod Y_i\to X$ would factor through some $Y_{I'}$.
With $X\supset\{0,1\}$ and $|I|>\pi$, $|Y_i|\ge2$: a subset such as the complement of a point is not the inverse image of a subset of a partial product. So no.
The opposite of $\mathbf{Ens}$ (of any topos) has direct limits and generators but is not accessible.
Also $\mathbf{Ab}^{\circ}$ is not accessible; all categories of structures of the kind studied here are.
E\ \text{and}\ E^{\circ}\ \text{both accessible}\ \overset{?}{\Longrightarrow}\ E\simeq\text{point}
Ind-objects
Main theorem of the story, for $E$ with small direct limits (probably filtering ones suffice).
First a model. $C$ small; $\mathbf{Ind}(C)$: filtering systems in $C$.
\mathbf{Ind}(C)\subset\widehat C=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C^\circ,\mathbf{Ens})\ \ \text{full},\qquad (X_i)\mapsto\varinjlim_{\widehat C}X_i
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ind}C}\big((X_i),(Y_j)\big)=\varprojlim_i\ \varinjlim_j\ \operatorname{Hom}_C(X_i,Y_j)
SGA 4, I, § 8 develops this formalism.
Universal property of $\mathbf{Ind}\,C$
$\mathbf{Cat}_\Delta$: categories with small filtering direct limits, functors commuting with them.
\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(\mathbf{Ind}\,C,E)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}(C,E)\qquad(\text{restriction along } C\to\mathbf{Ind}\,C)
$C\to\mathbf{Ind}\,C$: object $\mapsto$ constant system; i.e. the representable functor.
If $C$ has finite direct limits, $\mathbf{Ind}\,C$ has all direct limits.
\Delta'_0:\ \text{finite direct limits};\qquad \Delta':\ \text{all direct limits};\qquad C\in\Delta'_0\mapsto\mathbf{Ind}\,C\in\Delta'
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta'}(\mathbf{Ind}\,C,E)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta'_0}(C,E)\quad(\mathbf{Ind}\,C=\Delta'\text{-envelope of }C)
The categories $\mathbf{Ind}_\pi(C)$
C\subset\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C\subset\mathbf{Ind}\,C:\quad \text{ind-objects indexed by } \pi\text{-dominating } I
Claim: $\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C=:E$ is $\pi$-accessible. $C$ small, strictly generating: every object is a direct limit of a system in $C$.
Objects of $C$ are $\pi$-accessible: for $X\in C$,
Y\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\colon\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C\to\mathbf{Ens}\ \ \text{commutes with } \pi\text{-dominating direct limits}
Reduce to a system $(Y_\alpha)$, each $Y_\alpha$ a $\pi$-large system in $C$: fitting them together gives a double system, again $\pi$-large; direct limits commute with direct limits.
Recovering $C$ from $E$
X\in E\ \pi\text{-accessible}\iff X\ \text{is a direct factor of an object of } C
A direct factor of a $\pi$-accessible object is $\pi$-accessible. If $C$ is Karoubian (idempotents split), $E_\pi=C$.
Free modules over a ring: a direct factor need not be free — Karoubi envelope.
\mathbf{Ind}\,C=\mathbf{Ind}\,\bar C,\qquad \mathbf{Ind}_\pi C=\mathbf{Ind}_\pi\bar C\qquad(\bar C=\text{Karoubian envelope})
E=\mathbf{Ind}_\pi(E_\pi)
Cardinal filtration
\pi'\ge\pi:\quad \mathrm{Fil}^{\pi'}(E)=\{(X_i)_{i\in I}:\ I\ \pi\text{-dominating},\ |I|\le\pi'\}
$\mathrm{Fil}^{\pi}=C$. Claim: $\mathrm{Fil}^{\pi'}(E)=E_{\pi'}$, the $\pi'$-accessible objects.
Three properties — a cardinal filtration (SGA 4):
(1) each $\mathrm{Fil}^{\pi'}$ is essentially small;
(2) stable under direct limits over $I$ with $I$ $\pi$-dominating and $|I|\le\pi'$;
(3)\ \ \pi »\ge\pi':\ X\in\mathrm{Fil}^{\pi »}\Rightarrow X=\varinjlim_{i\in I}X_i,\ X_i\in\mathrm{Fil}^{\pi'},\ I\ \pi'\text{-dominating},\ |I|\le\pi »
(In SGA the bound was $\pi »^{\pi'}$: uglier, and unnecessary.)
Structure theorem for accessible categories
$E$ a category with direct limits, $\pi$ fixed. The following are equivalent:
a) $E$ is $\pi$-accessible.
\text{b)}\ \ E\simeq\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C\ \text{for a small category } C
c) $E_\pi$ is essentially small and strictly generating.
Chain: b) $\Rightarrow$ c) $\Rightarrow$ a); it remains to prove a) $\Rightarrow$ b).
Enlarge the small strictly generating $C\subset E_\pi$ to be stable under direct limits of cardinality $\le\pi$ (still small, still in $E_\pi$).
\hat\imath_\pi\colon\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C\to E\ \ \text{commutes with the relevant direct limits}
Fully faithful: because $C\subset E_\pi$.
Essentially surjective: $X=\varinjlim_{\alpha\in I}X_\alpha$ with $X_\alpha\in C$, perhaps not filtering.
X=\varinjlim_{I'}\Big(\varinjlim_{i\in I'}X_i\Big),\quad I'\subset I\ \text{subcategories with}\ |\mathrm{Ar}\,I'|\le\pi
The inner limits are in $C$ (stable); the outer system is $\pi$-dominating, so $X\in\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C$.
Uses existence of direct limits; without it the definition of accessibility may need changing.
Canonical choice: $C=E_\pi$.
(E_{\pi'})_{\pi'\ge\pi}\ \text{is a cardinal filtration;}\quad E\simeq\mathbf{Ind}_{\pi'}(E_{\pi'})
Accessible functors
$E,E'$ accessible: $E=\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C$, $E'=\mathbf{Ind}_\pi C'$.
F=\mathbf{Ind}_\pi(f),\qquad f\colon C=E_\pi\to C'=E'_\pi
False as stated: for $E=$ point every functor is $\pi$-accessible, but need not send the point into $E'_\pi$.
Correct form: fix $\pi_0$ with $E,E'$ both $\pi_0$-accessible.
F\ \text{accessible}\iff\exists\,\pi\ge\pi_0,\ f\colon E_\pi\to E'_\pi:\ F\simeq\mathbf{Ind}_\pi(f)
Converse: $E_{\pi_0}$ is small, so its image under $F$ is essentially small in $E'$, hence in some $E'_\pi$ (bounded cardinals of indexing sets).
Remaining: $F$ $\pi$-accessible and $F(E_{\pi_0})\subset E'_\pi$ give $F(E_\pi)\subset E'_\pi$? Perhaps need a larger cardinal.
\pi'>\pi:\quad X\in E_{\pi'}\Rightarrow X=\varinjlim_{I}X_i,\ X_i\in E_{\pi_0},\ |I|\le\pi'\ \Rightarrow\ F(X)\in E'_{\pi'}
